info.description: Enriched from `app.openapi()` by docs/api/tools/build_api_docs.py. Adds: servers, per-operation `x-hrms-*` metadata (permissions, rate limits, source), `Idempotency-Key` marked required where the dependency enforces it, and the shared error envelope on 4xx/5xx. FastAPI's generated schema alone under-reports these. Success responses are the generated ones, unmodified. Hand-written conventions: docs/api/API_OVERVIEW.md.

get.description:
RELEASE_HARDENING_PHASE_3B §7 — liveness answers "is this process alive?" only: no
database/Redis/storage check, so a dependency outage never causes an orchestrator to restart
an otherwise-healthy process (a restart storm that would make the outage worse, not better).
This is what `apps/api/Dockerfile`'s own `HEALTHCHECK` targets.

get.description:
Readiness answers "can this service actually serve production traffic?" — checks
PostgreSQL, Redis, and required object-storage configuration (RELEASE_HARDENING_PHASE_3B §7).
Returns HTTP 503 (not 200 with a "degraded" body) when not ready, since Nginx/an orchestrator
typically gates routing on status code rather than parsing the response body. Never returns
credentials, connection strings, or a stack trace — only ok/error per dependency.

post.description:
Closes the employee's current assignment row (if any) and inserts a new one — covers
initial placement, transfer, promotion, and manager change alike, distinguished only by
`change_type`. `If-Match` is required only when a current row exists (nothing to
version-check for an employee's very first assignment).

Unlike every other write route in this module, the gating permission is selected by the
request body's own `change_type` (module-header note above), so it cannot be expressed as a
static `Depends(require_permission(CODE))` — `rbac.resolve_data_scope()` is called directly
instead, mirroring `require_permission`'s own `_check_permission` helper
(`core/rbac/dependencies.py`) exactly: an empty `DataScope.levels` means the permission is
not held at all, `403`; a non-empty result both proves the permission is held and carries
the scope `create_assignment` must enforce against the target employee.

AccountInviteRead.title: AccountInviteRead
AccountInviteRead.description:
Returned by both issue endpoints — same "raw link is only ever available here" shape as
`OnboardingInviteRead` (only the token's SHA-256 hash is persisted).

AssignmentCreate.title: AssignmentCreate
AssignmentCreate.description:
Creates a new effective-dated assignment row — covers initial placement, transfer,
promotion, and manager change alike; all are the same insert-a-new-row operation,
distinguished only by `change_type` (plan §9). Every organisational reference field is
optional here even though `branch_id`/`department_id`/`designation_id` are mandatory for
an employee's very first assignment — when a current row exists, an omitted field carries
forward unchanged from it (`03_EMPLOYEE_API_PLAN.md` §2.2); the "required on first row"
rule is therefore enforced in the service, not this schema (plan §14.3).

AttendancePeriodBlockingReason.title: AttendancePeriodBlockingReason
AttendancePeriodBlockingReason.description:
One typed blocking bucket. `count` is the number of underlying rows/employees in this
bucket; `sample` carries up to 20 identifying values (employee ids, or `employee_id:date`
pairs) so the caller can navigate straight to the first few offenders without a second,
unbounded query.

AttendancePeriodCreate.title: AttendancePeriodCreate
AttendancePeriodCreate.description:
Create always opens immediately — no separate "open" action, mirroring WD-28's
no-DRAFT-state precedent (a period isn't useful in a created-but-not-open state; every date
inside it is mutable/computable from the instant it exists).

Decision 14 — one legal entity per period. Decision 18 — the cycle is a full calendar month
by default: send `month` (`YYYY-MM`) and the 1st-to-last-day range is derived from it (and a
"September 2026"-style label when none is given). An explicit `period_start`/`period_end`
pair is still accepted for an off-cycle period; send one form or the other, not both.

excess_break_days_to_half_day_count.title: Excess Break Days To Half Day Count
Excess Break Days To Half Day Count
Excess Break Days To Half Day Count

AttendanceRangeCalculateInput.title: AttendanceRangeCalculateInput
AttendanceRangeCalculateInput.description:
PAY-001 — backfill every employed day in `[date_from, date_to]` (company-local business
dates), optionally only for `employee_ids`.

BankCreate.title: BankCreate
BankCreate.description:
Creates a new effective-dated bank row — closes the employee's current row (if any) and
inserts a new one, mirroring `StatutoryCreate`'s write shape. Unlike Statutory, no
`revision_reason` field — no source document requires one for Banking
(`docs/modules/employee/33_EMPLOYEE_BANKING_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §5/§13).
`is_primary`/`verification_status`/`penny_drop_reference` are deliberately absent —
system-managed, never client-writable (plan §13).

CalendarExceptionUpdate.title: CalendarExceptionUpdate
CalendarExceptionUpdate.description:
Never accepts `exception_date`/`exception_type` — corrections are deactivate-then-
insert (architecture §7.3), matching `HolidayUpdate`'s immutable-date posture.

CalendarResolutionRead.title: CalendarResolutionRead
CalendarResolutionRead.description:
Response for `GET /calendar-resolution?employee_id=&date=` — the full WD-09 precedence
walk plus the resulting day-type classification, or `config_incomplete=true` (fail-closed,
WD-21) when no WorkCalendar resolves for this employee+date.

CompanyDashboardSummary.title: CompanyDashboardSummary
CompanyDashboardSummary.description:
Stable dashboard DTO — sibling counts stay null until those modules ship
(04_API_Design.md §7). Additive optional fields may be added later without
breaking this contract.

CompensationCreate.title: CompensationCreate
CompensationCreate.description:
Creates a new effective-dated compensation row — closes the employee's current row (if
any) and inserts a new one. Unlike `AssignmentCreate`, no field carries forward from the
current row: `annual_ctc_minor`, `currency`, `revision_type`, and `revision_reason` are
always required, on every write, including an employee's very first compensation row
(plan §17.2/§17.3) — a stale CTC carried forward by omission is a materially worse failure
mode than a stale org-placement field.

DayTypeRead.title: DayTypeRead
DayTypeRead.description:
Computed classification of a single date against a WorkCalendar — never persisted (no
`AttendanceDay` exists yet). See `calendar_resolution.classify_work_calendar_date`.

EmployeeConfirmInput.title: EmployeeConfirmInput
EmployeeConfirmInput.description:
`POST /employees/{id}/confirm` — transitions `PROBATION` -> `ACTIVE`. No fields: unlike
`EmploymentTerminate` (which needs `last_working_day`), confirmation needs no input at all —
the before/after `Employee.status` values in the audit record are the entire story. Kept as
an explicit (empty) body model rather than no body, matching every other action in this
router.

EmployeeDocumentRead.title: EmployeeDocumentRead
EmployeeDocumentRead.description:
Deliberately excludes `s3_key`/`source_onboarding_document_id` — internal storage/
provenance details, never returned to a caller.

EmployeeDocumentWithUrlRead.title: EmployeeDocumentWithUrlRead
EmployeeDocumentWithUrlRead.description:
Adds the short-lived presigned GET URL — document bytes never round-trip through the API
server. Returned to every caller who can list documents at all (HR/Admin and the SELF-scoped
employee alike): unlike onboarding's candidate-facing `list_documents` (no URL, because an
unreviewed candidate upload might still be replaced), every viewer here is already permitted
to download what they can see.

EmployeeSalaryBreakupRead.title: EmployeeSalaryBreakupRead
EmployeeSalaryBreakupRead.description:
An employee's pay as of a date: the structure breakup for a monthly-paid employee, or the
daily rate for a daily-wage one (D5) — `breakup` is `None` then.

EmployeeSalaryBulkAssign.title: EmployeeSalaryBulkAssign
EmployeeSalaryBulkAssign.description:
Assign one structure to monthly-paid employees who have no salary assignment covering
`effective_from` — the one-off step that lets existing employees reach their first pay run.
Without `employee_ids`, every such employee employed on that date.

EmploymentCreate.title: EmploymentCreate
EmploymentCreate.description:
Creates a new employment episode for an existing employee — covers both a first hire
(no prior employment rows) and a rehire (at least one prior, necessarily `TERMINATED`,
episode exists). The distinction is not client-supplied: `previous_employment_id` is
always computed server-side from the employee's own employment history, never accepted as
input (`status`/`version` are likewise system-set, never client-settable).

`probation_end_date` is optional and purely informational — nothing reads or auto-computes
it; the actual `PROBATION` -> `ACTIVE` transition is the explicit `confirm` action, never
gated by this date.

EmploymentUpdate.title: EmploymentUpdate
EmploymentUpdate.description:
Only `legal_entity_id` and `probation_end_date` are correctable post-creation.
`joining_date` is a historical fact once recorded (no document states it is ever
legitimately revised, and every other slice in this codebase treats a spell's start as
immutable); `status`/`last_working_day` only ever change via the dedicated `terminate`
action, never a generic field patch — this keeps the one-way `ACTIVE` → `TERMINATED`
transition from being reachable through an unvalidated arbitrary-field update.
`probation_end_date` is the one exception to "immutable once set": it's purely
informational bookkeeping, not a fact anything downstream depends on, so HR correcting it
carries none of `joining_date`'s risk.

FaceEnrollmentStatusRead.title: FaceEnrollmentStatusRead
FaceEnrollmentStatusRead.description:
Everything a screen needs to decide what to show: the profile (if any) and the currently
usable enrollment window (OPEN and unexpired), if any.

FaceLivenessSessionRead.title: FaceLivenessSessionRead
FaceLivenessSessionRead.description:
`POST /attendance/face-punches/me/liveness-sessions` — the single-use challenge the next
face punch must present, and how many frames it must carry.

FaceProfileRead.title: FaceProfileRead
FaceProfileRead.description:
Never exposes `provider_person_id` (a handle into the vendor's biometric store) or the
review photo's storage key.

FacePunchRead.title: FacePunchRead
FacePunchRead.description: `POST /attendance/face-punches/me` — the punch recorded plus the scores that justified it.

HolidayUpdate.title: HolidayUpdate
HolidayUpdate.description:
Never accepts `date`/`calendar_id` — a holiday's date is immutable after creation
(architecture §25: "no PATCH of used dates"). Correcting a wrong date is deactivate this
row + create a new one, preserving history.

LeaveApplicationCancelInput.title: LeaveApplicationCancelInput
LeaveApplicationCancelInput.description:
Optional body for cancel. `reason` is mandatory when HR cancels an approved application
that has already started (decision 10); recorded whenever given.

LeaveApplicationCreate.title: LeaveApplicationCreate
LeaveApplicationCreate.description:
Shared by self-submit and on-behalf-submit (router decides `employee_id`, mirrors
`RegularizationRequestCreate`'s convention). `half_day` is only valid for a single-day
application (`start_date == end_date`) — this first cut does not support a half-day
boundary on a multi-day range (e.g. half day at the start, full days between, half day at
the end); every day in a multi-day range is a full day or a sandwich-rule-generated day.

LeaveApplicationReassignInput.title: LeaveApplicationReassignInput
LeaveApplicationReassignInput.description: Decision 13 - HR hands a stuck approval stage to another approver. `reason` is mandatory.

LeaveApplicationReviewInput.title: LeaveApplicationReviewInput
LeaveApplicationReviewInput.description:
Body for approve/reject — mirrors `RegularizationReviewInput` exactly. `rejection_reason`
is only meaningful on reject; ignored (not an error) if supplied on approve.

LeaveBalanceRead.title: LeaveBalanceRead
LeaveBalanceRead.description:
One row per leave type that `requires_balance` — a type with zero ledger activity still
appears, with `balance=0`, rather than being silently omitted.

`balance` (LD-03's derived ledger sum, "Available Balance" in the client's own terminology)
is never reduced by a pending application unless `reserve_balance_on_submission` is enabled
for it — `reserved_balance` (LD-15) is always shown alongside it regardless, so HR/employee
can see both figures separately (client spec §8) even when reservation itself is off.

LeaveCombinationRuleCreate.title: LeaveCombinationRuleCreate
LeaveCombinationRuleCreate.description: `leave_type_id_a`/`_b` may be given in either order — the pair is unordered (LD-16).

LeaveLedgerAdjustmentCreate.title: LeaveLedgerAdjustmentCreate
LeaveLedgerAdjustmentCreate.description:
Input for a manual HR balance correction, writing a generic `ADJUSTMENT` entry
(ACCRUAL/APPLICATION/CARRY_FORWARD/COMP_OFF_CREDIT are reserved for L3/L4/L5; `ENCASHMENT`
has its own dedicated, validated path — `LeaveLedgerEncashmentCreate` below, LD-19).
`employee_id` lives in the body, mirroring `RegularizationRequestCreate`'s convention, not a
query param.

LeaveLedgerEncashmentCreate.title: LeaveLedgerEncashmentCreate
LeaveLedgerEncashmentCreate.description:
Input for L2.5's dedicated encashment path (client spec §12, LD-19) — `days` is always
positive (the amount encashed, debited from balance), unlike `LeaveLedgerAdjustmentCreate.
amount`'s signed shape. Validated against the applicable `LeavePolicyVersion`'s
`encashment_allowed`/`max_encashment_days`/`min_balance_after_encashment` before writing an
`ENCASHMENT` entry — never a bare unvalidated adjustment.

LeaveProjectionSync.title: LeaveProjectionSync
LeaveProjectionSync.description:
Publishes (or republishes) one approved leave day projection — architecture §21's
`LeaveDayProjection` read model.

LM-14: the body only *identifies* the day (`employee_id` + `leave_application_id` +
`attendance_date`). Leave type, fraction, half and paid/unpaid are always taken from the
APPROVED `LeaveApplicationDay` in the Leave module; the optional fields below are accepted
for backward compatibility and IGNORED, so a caller can never contradict the approved leave.
The cross-row "active fractions for this employee-date must not exceed 1.00" check still
happens in the service layer, on the authoritative fraction.

LeaveYearSettingUpsert.title: LeaveYearSettingUpsert
LeaveYearSettingUpsert.description:
`start_month`/`start_day` only apply to `CUSTOM` — required together when
`leave_year_type=CUSTOM`, ignored (must be omitted) otherwise, since `CALENDAR`/`FINANCIAL`
have fixed, non-configurable start dates and `ANNIVERSARY` has no company-wide date at all
(LD-20).

OnboardingCaseDetailRead.title: OnboardingCaseDetailRead
OnboardingCaseDetailRead.description:
`GET /onboarding-cases/{id}` (admin) — extends the list-safe `OnboardingCaseRead` with the
five section JSON blobs and their review status, so HR can actually see what the candidate
submitted, not just verify/reject blind (plan §9: "per-section review cards"). Deliberately
not folded into `OnboardingCaseRead` itself — that shape is also used by `GET
/onboarding-cases` (the list view), which has no business returning bank-account/statutory
detail for every row on a list screen.

OnboardingDocumentRead.title: OnboardingDocumentRead
OnboardingDocumentRead.description:
Deliberately excludes `s3_key` — an internal storage detail, never returned to either the
candidate or the admin UI (which gets a presigned URL instead, `OnboardingDocumentWithUrlRead`
below).

OnboardingDocumentWithUrlRead.title: OnboardingDocumentWithUrlRead
OnboardingDocumentWithUrlRead.description:
The admin-only shape (`GET /onboarding-cases/{id}/documents`) — adds the short-lived
presigned GET URL so document bytes never round-trip through the API server (plan §8.3).

OnboardingInviteRead.title: OnboardingInviteRead
OnboardingInviteRead.description:
`POST /onboarding-cases/{id}/send-invite` (O3) — returns the updated case plus the raw
`invite_url`, since this response is the *only* time the raw link is ever available (only
its token's SHA-256 hash is persisted, plan §8.1). This is also what backs the admin UI's
"Copy link" action (plan §9) independent of whether `email_sent` succeeded — a failed email
delivery must not block HR from getting the link some other way.

OvertimeReviewInput.title: OvertimeReviewInput
OvertimeReviewInput.description: Body for approve/reject — identical shape to `RegularizationReviewInput`.

PayAdjustmentCreate.title: PayAdjustmentCreate
PayAdjustmentCreate.description:

legal entity's next pay run.

PayRunCreate.title: PayRunCreate
PayRunCreate.description:
`month` is `YYYY-MM` — a pay run always covers one whole calendar month (decision 18).
`pay_date` defaults to the first weekday of the following month (D11).

PayRunEmployeeDetailRead.title: PayRunEmployeeDetailRead
PayRunEmployeeDetailRead.description:
One employee's pay in a run: the totals, every line with its trace, and the input
snapshot the figures were computed from.

PayRunRollback.title: PayRunRollback
PayRunRollback.description: Back to `DRAFT` (drops the snapshot) or `INPUTS_LOCKED` (drops the computed pay).

PayslipRead.title: PayslipRead
PayslipRead.description:
One employee's payslip for one pay run (FR-PAY-017). `is_final` is false for an HR preview
of a run not yet finalised — employees only ever see final ones.

PublicAccountInviteRead.title: PublicAccountInviteRead
PublicAccountInviteRead.description:
Shown by the public `GET .../{token}` route before the accept form — enough for the
invitee to recognize what they're accepting, nothing more (no role/permission detail).

`existing_account` (SEC-08) tells the frontend whether `POST .../accept` will create a new
account or authenticate an existing one — the invitee's own email is already known to them
(it's the address the invite was sent to), so surfacing this is not an enumeration risk; it
lets the accept form ask for a login password instead of a new one.

PublicOnboardingCaseRead.title: PublicOnboardingCaseRead
PublicOnboardingCaseRead.description:
`GET /public/onboarding/{token}` — deliberately narrower than `OnboardingCaseRead`: no
`id`/`company_id`/`created_by_user_id`/`employee_id` (the candidate has no use for internal
IDs and no session to authorize looking anything else up with), and `writable` tells the
wizard which sections it may currently `PATCH` (module docstring,
`ONBOARDING_CASE_WRITABLE_STATUSES`). `section_reviews` (O6) lets the wizard show which
sections HR has already verified (lock the fields, nothing left to fix) versus rejected (show
the reason) — deliberately just `section`/`status`/`rejection_reason`, no reviewer identity or
timestamp, which the candidate has no use for.

PublicTokenResponseData.title: PublicTokenResponseData
PublicTokenResponseData.description:
SEC-06 (RELEASE_HARDENING_PHASE_3A) — the actual HTTP response shape for every
token-issuing endpoint (login, refresh, registration, invite acceptance): identical to
`TokenResponseData` minus `refresh_token`, which travels only as an HttpOnly cookie
(`hrms.core.auth.refresh_cookie.set_refresh_cookie`).

PunchCreateOnBehalf.title: PunchCreateOnBehalf
PunchCreateOnBehalf.description:
Body for `POST /attendance/punches` — HR/admin entering a punch for someone else
(`ATTENDANCE.PUNCH_ON_BEHALF`).

Client-supplied time is **required** here, because that is the workflow's entire purpose:
recording an instant the server did not itself observe. It is bounded rather than trusted —
not in the future (`FuturePunchTimeError`), not inside a `CLOSED` period (`_ensure_date_open`),
not before the employee's employment began (`PunchTimeBeforeEmploymentError`).

`reference` is the **reason** and is mandatory here (it stays optional on the self route),
so every administrative override carries its own justification into the audit log.

`source` is absent by design and server-assigned as `ADMIN`, closing `F-11`: the value can no
longer be chosen by the caller on any route.

PunchCreateSelf.title: PunchCreateSelf
PunchCreateSelf.description:
Body for `POST /attendance/punches/me` — employee self-service (`DEC-TZ-01`, SELECTED).

**There is deliberately no `punch_time`, no `source`, and no `employee_id` field here.** The
punch instant is the moment the server receives the request; the source is assigned from the
authenticated route; the employee is the caller. Under `extra="forbid"` a client that sends
any of the three gets a 422 rather than being quietly ignored, so an old client fails loudly
instead of silently having its timestamp discarded.

This is why no clock-skew tolerance is configurable anywhere in the module: with no
client-supplied instant on this path there is nothing to compare a tolerance against. The
control is structural, not a threshold (execution gate §7.1).

ReadinessData.title: ReadinessData
ReadinessData.description:
Dependency-aware — distinct from `HealthData`/`/health` (unchanged, kept for backward
compatibility with existing callers) and from liveness (`/health/live`, no dependency checks
at all). Consumed by Nginx/an orchestrator to decide whether to route traffic here, not by
Docker's own container `HEALTHCHECK` (that targets `/health/live` — see `apps/api/Dockerfile`
— precisely so a dependency outage doesn't trigger container restart storms).

RegistrationConfigRead.title: RegistrationConfigRead
RegistrationConfigRead.description:
Body for the public, unauthenticated `GET /companies/registration-config` — lets the
sign-up page narrow its timezone `<select>` to what the server will actually accept, fetched
from the API rather than duplicated as a second, independently-maintained TypeScript list
(execution gate §6.3: "two independently maintained lists is how they drift"). Read-only;
changing the allowed set is a `settings.allowed_company_timezones` configuration change, not
a schema change.

RegularizationRequestCreate.title: RegularizationRequestCreate
RegularizationRequestCreate.description:
Shared by self-submit and on-behalf-submit (router decides `employee_id` — architecture
§23.2: self is SELF-scoped, on-behalf is COMPANY-scoped). WD-28 decision 2: every request
must carry `requested_punches` and/or `requested_shift_id` so an approval always has a
well-defined, engine-supported effect.

Note this schema keeps the single-endpoint, body-decides-`employee_id` shape that the punch
routes deliberately moved away from in Phase 1 (`ED-4`). That is intentional and not an
oversight: regularization is approval-gated end to end, so the body cannot select a
*privilege* here the way it could on the punch path — the reviewer, not the submitter,
decides whether anything is written.

RegularizationRequestedPunchInput.title: RegularizationRequestedPunchInput
RegularizationRequestedPunchInput.description:
One requested IN/OUT instant — reuses `_PUNCH_DIRECTIONS` verbatim (WD-12: don't
redefine a second direction enum).

`requested_time` carries the same `AwareIsoDatetime` contract as the on-behalf punch route:
regularization is the *other* legitimately client-time-accepting path (execution gate §7.2),
so it gets the identical wire guard rather than a weaker one. It stays approval-gated — the
instant only becomes a `punch` row once a reviewer approves it.

RegularizationReviewInput.title: RegularizationReviewInput
RegularizationReviewInput.description:
Body for approve/reject. `rejection_reason` is only meaningful (and only persisted) on
reject; the service ignores it on approve rather than erroring, since a caller-supplied
but-unused field on the wrong action is not itself invalid input.

RoleAssignmentRequest.title: RoleAssignmentRequest
RoleAssignmentRequest.description:

SalaryStructureVersionCreate.title: SalaryStructureVersionCreate

ShiftBreakCreate.title: ShiftBreakCreate
ShiftBreakCreate.description:

independent lifecycle, no standalone endpoint (full-replace only). `crosses_midnight` is
not client-settable — server-derived from the time comparison, same posture as
`ShiftVersion.is_cross_midnight`.

ShiftCreate.title: ShiftCreate
ShiftCreate.description:

legacy `Shift` used to accept here now live on `ShiftVersion`
(docs/architecture/WORKFORCE_ATTENDANCE_ARCHITECTURE.md §9-§10).

ShiftDutyBlockCreate.title: ShiftDutyBlockCreate
ShiftDutyBlockCreate.description:

SPLIT shift types only, no independent lifecycle. `crosses_midnight` is not
client-settable — server-derived from the time comparison.

ShiftRead.title: ShiftRead
ShiftRead.description:
The nine legacy schedule/evaluation fields below are **deprecated, read-only, and
frozen at W2-migration time** — kept for audit/back-compat continuity only, never written
again by W2+ code (superseded by `ShiftVersion`/`ShiftBreak`, see field-level
descriptions). `current_version_id`/`draft_version_id` are cheap lookups so a caller knows
schedule state without a second round trip.

ShiftRosterBulkCreate.title: ShiftRosterBulkCreate
ShiftRosterBulkCreate.description:
Covers the brief's "fixed roster" (repeat one shift across a date range, expanded
client-side into `entries`) and "monthly roster" (an explicit date→shift list) — no
rotation-pattern generator is built server-side (WD-27); the backend only ever sees dated
rows, matching the architecture's typed/no-generic-engine posture (WD-12).

ShiftVersionCreate.title: ShiftVersionCreate
ShiftVersionCreate.description:
Creates a new open DRAFT `ShiftVersion` for a shift (409
`SHIFT_VERSION_DRAFT_ALREADY_EXISTS` if one is already open). All fields are optional —
a draft may be incomplete mid-edit; only `POST .../publish` enforces the full,
type-specific field set. `is_cross_midnight` is never client-settable — always
server-derived from the time fields. `is_night_shift` IS client-settable: architecture
§9.5 is explicit that it "is an explicit flag (night OT classification), not inferred
solely from times" — unlike `is_cross_midnight`, which the same section says "must be
consistent with start/end (already validated)".

ShiftVersionPublishRequest.title: ShiftVersionPublishRequest
ShiftVersionPublishRequest.description:
Body for `POST /shifts/{shift_id}/versions/{version_id}/publish`. `If-Match` (header,
handled at the router layer) carries the draft's own `expected_version`;
`expected_previous_version` is the **second** concurrency token in this two-token flow —
required only when an open PUBLISHED version already exists for this shift, so it can be
closed as part of the same publish (mirrors `create_policy_assignment`'s insert-new/
close-previous idiom exactly, just with two tokens instead of one since two different rows
are being mutated).

ShiftVersionUpdate.title: ShiftVersionUpdate
ShiftVersionUpdate.description:
Draft-only PATCH (409 `SHIFT_VERSION_NOT_DRAFT` once published). `breaks`/
`duty_blocks`, when present, **replace** the entire nested collection atomically — no
separate sub-resource CRUD, since they have no independent lifecycle (mirrors
`WeeklyOffPatternUpdate.rules`).

StatutoryCreate.title: StatutoryCreate
StatutoryCreate.description:
Creates a new effective-dated statutory row — closes the employee's current row (if
any) and inserts a new one, mirroring `CompensationCreate` exactly: no field carries
forward from the current row, `revision_reason` is required on every write (plan §16/§27
item 7), including an employee's very first statutory row.

StatutoryLeaveMinimumCreate.title: StatutoryLeaveMinimumCreate
StatutoryLeaveMinimumCreate.description:
`state_code`/`establishment_type` are optional narrowing dimensions, not required
identifiers — `None` on either means "applies regardless of that dimension" (LD-22).

StatutoryRateCreate.title: StatutoryRateCreate
StatutoryRateCreate.description:
A new effective-dated rate. When a rate for the same scheme and state is open, it ends the
day before `effective_from`.

UserInviteRequest.title: UserInviteRequest
UserInviteRequest.description:
